LIME provides local explanations centered on the top-1 prediction, helping validate feature impacts. Integrated gradients offer smooth, gradient-based attributions across the input space for better consistency. Sensitivity analysis directly measures how probability shifts when features are altered, offering empirical validation of feature influence in contrastive settings.

The input features show 'HS-grad', 'State-gov', and 'Male', which are less common in the >50K group according to historical patterns. result.explanation: Based on domain knowledge and historical patterns in income prediction datasets (e.g., the Census Income Dataset), several features are strongly correlated with income >50K. Higher education levels (e.g., education-num ≥ 13) are associated with greater income potential. Working in private sector (vs. government or state-funded) is often linked to higher earnings. Age is positively correlated with income up to a point (mid-50s), though diminishing returns apply. Higher hours-per-week (e.g., >40) are indicative of higher earning potential. Additionally, gender has historically shown a correlation, with males historically earning more than females in such datasets, so changing to 'Female' demonstrates how the feature affects the model's confidence in predicting >50K. The current feature values—such as 'State-gov' workclass, low education-num, and male sex—are more typical of lower-income groups. Adjusting these to values known to correlate with higher income strengthens the distinction between >50K and ≤50K predictions.
